system.name: GRANNY
system.one_liner: a runtime for granular management of compute-intensive cloud applications that cross-compiles code to WebAssembly and virtualizes OpenMP/MPI/POSIX backends

components.name: Granule
components.role: an OS thread inside the VM running isolated WebAssembly application code, the unit GRANNY manages

components.name: Thread + CGroup + Net NS
components.role: OS-level isolation mechanisms wrapping a Granule

components.name: Application code (WebAssembly)
components.role: memory-safe, platform-independent application binary, cross-compiled to WebAssembly, restricted to pre-defined backend operations

components.name: Control point
components.role: boundary at which application code calls into a supported runtime backend API, where GRANNY intercepts control

components.name: MPI backend
components.role: implements MPI_* operations (e.g., MPI_Barrier) for Granules

components.name: POSIX backend
components.role: implements fd_*, mmap, and other POSIX operations for Granules

components.name: OMP backend
components.role: implements kmpc*/omp* OpenMP operations for Granules

components.name: Granny core
components.role: shared runtime core keeping per-Granule state (message mailboxes, FD tables, SHM mappings) and decoupling backends from the OS

components.name: Message mailboxes
components.role: per-Granule mailbox structure used by the MPI backend for message passing

components.name: FD tables
components.role: mapping between WebAssembly file descriptors and OS file descriptors, maintained by the POSIX backend

components.name: SHM mappings
components.role: shared-memory mappings used by the OMP backend

components.name: Granny runtime
components.role: runtime layer hosting the three backends and the Granny core, decoupling Granules from the host OS

components.name: Linux
components.role: host OS providing net, fs, threads, ns, and cgroups primitives that the Granny runtime relies on via system calls

flows.what: calls to supported runtime backend APIs (OpenMP, MPI, POSIX)

summary: GRANNY manages compute-intensive applications in the cloud at the granularity of a 'Granule': an OS thread, wrapped in a Thread+CGroup+NetNS sandbox, running application code cross-compiled to WebAssembly. Figure 2 shows this as a layered stack: application code can only reach the outside world through a Control point into one of three color-coded Granny runtime backends -- MPI backend, POSIX backend, and OMP backend -- all built on a shared Granny core that keeps per-Granule state (message mailboxes, FD tables, SHM mappings) and decouples the backends from the OS. The Granny runtime then defers to the host Linux kernel's net, fs, threads, ns, and cgroups facilities via ordinary system calls. This design lets Granules execute side by side in one address space while GRANNY intercepts every backend call as a control point for scheduling and migration.
